 HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. AJAI LAMBA
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SOUMITRA SAIKIA

 ORDER

Date : 25-02-2020
(Ajai Lamba, C.J.)

1. In deference to order dated 11.02.2020, a sum of ` 15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen
 Thousand) has been handed over by the appellant/husband to the respondent/wife, who are
 both present in Court.

2. The application has been filed by Smti. Bani Mochari under Section 8 read with
 Section 10A of the Divorce Act, 1869 (for short, "Act of 1869") to consider the matter and
 dissolve the marriage by mutual consent.
3. Section 8 of the Act of 1869 reads as under:-

"8. Extraordinary jurisdiction of High Court. - The High Court may, whenever
 it thinks fit, remove and try and determine as a Court of original jurisdiction any suit
 or proceeding instituted under this Act in the Court of any District Judge within the
 limits of its jurisdiction under this Act."
4. Section 10A of the Act of 1869 reads as under:-

"10A. Dissolution of marriage by mutual consent. - (1) Subject to the provisions of
 this Act and the rules made thereunder, a petition for dissolution of marriage may be
 presented to the District Court by both the parties to a marriage together, whether
 such marriage was solemnized before or after the commencement* of the Indian
 Divorce (Amendment) Act, 2001, on the ground that they have been living separately
 for a period of two years or more, that they have not been able to live together and
 they have mutually agreed that the marriage should be dissolved.

(2) On the motion of both the parties made not earlier than six months after the date
 of presentation of the petition referred to in sub-section (1) and not later than
 eighteen months after the said date, if the petition is not withdrawn by both the
 Page No.# 3/4

 parties in the meantime, the Court shall, on being satisfied, after hearing the parties
 and making such inquiry, as it thinks fit, that a marriage has been solemnized and
 that the averments in the petition are true, pass a decree declaring the marriage to
 be dissolved with effect from the date of decree."

5. We have taken judicial notice of the fact that the parties are Christians. The
husband Shri Salil Mochari filed F.C. (Civil) No.37/2014 in the Court of Principal Judge, Family
Court No.2, Kamrup (Metro), Guwahati under Section 10(ix) of the Act of 1869 on ground of
cruelty. Vide the judgment dated 06.09.2017, the suit was dismissed.

6. Aggrieved by decision dated 06.09.2017, the respondent/husband preferred
Matrimonial Appeal No.11/2018.

7. Having referred to the order-sheet, we find that attempts were made at
reconciliation. Even the children of the parties were summoned, however, the disputes could
not be resolved.

8. It appears that considering various aspects of the case, the application has been
filed at the instance of the wife for dissolution of marriage by mutual consent for the
extensive reasons given in the application.

9. It has been pleaded on behalf of the wife, and not disputed by the husband that
the marriage of the parties was solemnized in the year 1995. There are 2(two) children out
of the wedlock, the elder being a son aged 22 years, and the younger being a daughter
aged 9 years. It is further not in dispute that the conjugal life of the parties came to an end
in July, 2011, whereafter the parties have been living separately. At this point in time, both
the children are living with their mother.

10. It transpires that the wife is being given maintenance under Section 125 Cr.PC in
the sum of ` 10,000/- per month for support of her children. The amount initially assessed
by Judicial Magistrate, Kokrajhar was ` 3,500/-, which was revised to ` 5,500/- and from
` 5,500/- to ` 10,000/-, which is being paid as on date.

11. It has been stated in the application and not disputed by the respondent, who are
both present in Court, that several attempts at reunion were made, however, all the
attempts failed. It has been pleaded on behalf of both the sides that because reunion is not
possible considering various aspects of the case, it would be in the best interest of both the
 Page No.# 4/4

 sides, and also the children for their future that the issue is settled once and for all. It has
 been projected before the Court that although technically and legally the parties are
 married, however, have been living separate for the last about 9(nine) years. In such
 circumstances, it has been prayed that the matter be considered as one under Section 10A 
 of the Act of 1869.

12. Considering various aspects of the case, and in particular the statement given by
 the parties, we deem it appropriate to deal with this matter as one under Section 10A of the
 Act of 1869.

13. We find that all the conditions mentioned under Section 10A of the Act of 1869
 stand satisfied. We are of the considered view that the reunion of the parties is not possible.
 It is an irretrievably broken marriage.

14. Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, we hereby allow the
 application.
15. The marriage between the parties is hereby dissolved by mutual consent.

Judgment dated 06.09.2017 rendered in F.C. (Civil) No.37/2014 is hereby set
 aside.

16. So far as alimony is concerned, the wife would be at liberty to file an application
 under Section 37 of the Act of 1869 before the appropriate forum. Needless to say that the
 maintenance being paid under Section 125 Cr.PC would continue as per the directions of the
 Court concerned, unless that Court rules otherwise.

17. With the above observations and directions, matrimonial appeal as well as the
 interlocutory application stand allowed.
18. Registry is directed to send back the lower Court record.

JUDGE CHIEF JUSTICE
